defects: Hypothesis is not equivalent to gold's UniqueMul: produced uses ∃! (p : M × M), p.1 ∈ supp f ∧ p.2 ∈ supp g ∧ p.1*p.2 = a0*b0, which asserts existence of a (unique) decomposition of a0*b0 but never requires that decomposition to actually be the pair (a0,b0). Gold's UniqueMul f.coeff.support g.coeff.support a0 b0 is defined as ∀ a b, a∈s → b∈t → a*b=a0*b0 → a=a0 ∧ b=b0, which (a) holds vacuously when a0∉supp f or b0∉supp g (no decomposition needed) and (b) forces any existing decomposition to equal (a0,b0). These two hypotheses are logically independent: e.g. with M=(ℕ,+), a0=5, b0=3, supp f={1}, supp g={7} (1+7=8=a0+b0 the unique such decomposition) satisfies the produced hypothesis but not UniqueMul, and the conclusion generally fails (LHS = f.coeff 1 * g.coeff 7 ≠ 0 = f.coeff 5 * g.coeff 3 = RHS), showing the produced statement is not a faithful (indeed not even a true) formalization.
Produced adds an extra/stronger typeclass assumption [Monoid M] (associativity + identity) in place of gold's [Mul A], unnecessarily narrowing the generality of the statement.
